name: Six advantages
oneLine: Every game pays out on six channels at once: internal and external psychological, internal and external social, biological, and existential.
whatYouDid: You wrote out the six advantages for one of Omar, Leah, Divya, or Farid's games - the obvious payoff (a bad feeling) is only one piece; the rest (avoided anxiety, a theme for gossip, a guaranteed supply of strokes, confirmation of a life position) are easy to miss.
confusion: People spot the one obvious gain - usually the racket feeling, or the stroke supply - and stop there, missing that Berne counted six separate advantages running at once, several of which look nothing like a "payoff."

fromBook.quote: In Games People Play, Eric Berne listed 'six advantages' of game-playing.

expand.definition: (1) Internal psychological: stabilizes your script beliefs. (2) External psychological: lets you avoid a challenge to your frame of reference. (3) Internal social: a framework for pseudo-intimate exchanges in private. (4) External social: a theme for gossip in your wider circle. (5) Biological: a reliable supply of strokes, positive or negative. (6) Existential: confirms your basic life position.
expand.otherFraming: John James added a seventh idea on top of Berne's six: every game also has a hidden positive payoff for the Child, separate from the scripty negative one - the trick is finding it and meeting that real need in a straight way instead.
expand.tryThisToday: Take one game you play more than once a month and name all six advantages in writing - the external social one, what you get to gossip about afterward, is usually the one people forget.
